title: Veterinary Anesthesia Laboratory
description: The veterinary technician's role in patient assessment, preparation, induction, monitoring, maintenance, and recovery of anesthesia. Includes sedation, analgesia, general anesthesia, and local anesthesia techniques, in addition to practical applications of pharmacology. Skills pertaining to anesthesia will be practiced. Intended for students in the Veterinary Technology Program; enrollment is limited to students accepted in the program.
outcomes: Competently perform a full dental cleaning and maintain sterility while assist a surgeon during routine spays and neuters.
Safely and competently prepare, induce, maintain, and recover and provide post procedure care for dogs and cats from general anesthesia for spays and neuters
objectives: Describe the role of the veterinary technician during the anesthetic event.
Perform a thorough pre-anesthetic evaluation of a veterinary patient and develop a comprehensive anesthetic plan.
Perform a thorough post-anesthetic evaluation of a veterinary patient and develop a nursing care plan.
Identify and explain the function of each of the components of the veterinary anesthesia machine.
Recognize, critically evaluate, and respond appropriately to common anesthetic problems and emergencies.
Describe the effects of anesthesia on the nervous, cardiovascular, and respiratory systems.
Demonstrate the essential clinical skills related to anesthesiology.
Explain general principles of inhalation anesthesia and successfully manage a veterinary patient.
Demonstrate competence in the induction, monitoring, maintenance, and recovery of a veterinary patient under inhalant anesthesia.
Demonstrate competency in the use of manual methods of ventilation.
Participate in four common surgeries in small animal practice.
Participate in a minimum of one complete oral health assessment and treatment under anesthesia for a dog or a cat.
content: Role of the veterinary technician in anesthesia
Pre-anesthetic evaluation and development of comprehensive anesthetic plan
Appropriate laboratory testing using equipment commonly found in clinical practices (CBC, chemistry analyzer, PCV, TP)
Animal care to program standards, based on the Animal Welfare Act
Critical considerations in the recovery period
Components, function, and use of the anesthetic machine
Effects of anesthesia on the nervous, cardiovascular, and respiratory systems
Physical parameters (TPR, mucous membrane color, CRT, jaw tone, reflexes, eye position)
Essential clinical skills related to anesthesiology
Calculation of fluid rates and volumes
Fluid rates for different times of anesthesia
Patient preparation for dog spay, cat spay, dog neuter, cat neuter surgical procedures
Principles of inhalation anesthesia and successfully manage a veterinary patient
Dental prophylaxis (complete oral health assessment and treatment or COHAT)
Suturing and appropriate handling of live tissue
Surgical scrubbing; donning and doffing of PPE (gowns and gloves)
Oral health assessment and treatment under anesthesia for a dog or a cat
lab: Laboratory content will closely follow the course outline of record. Students will be in anesthesia groups and work on live animals under direct supervision in performing the following tasks:
